text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Algeria bought 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat from two trade houses at between $183 and $184 a tonne including freight, European grain traders said. The four wheat cargoes, for May/June shipment, could come at least partly from France despite the reported exclusion of French firms from recent Algerian tenders.
WHEAT BRAN SALE - South Korean buyer groups, the Korea Feed Association and the Big Feed Mills, jointly bought 81,950 tonnes Indonesian wheat bran pellet from Bogasari.

SOYOIL SALE - Tunisia bought a total of 27,000 tonnes of soybean oil at a tender on Thursday, European vegetable oil traders said. The purchase was split into three shipment periods. In the first lot, due to arrive between May 5-15, 6,000 tonnes of soy oil was purchased at $548, 3,000 tonnes at $546.50 and 3,000 tonnes at $547. The second shipment was due to arrive June 1-10 with 6,000 tonnes bought at $548, 3,000 at $549 and 3,000 at $548. Arrival for the third shipment of 3,000 tonnes was July 20-30 and the purchase price for this parcel was $549 a tonne c and f. Traders also said Morocco passed on a tender.

BARLEY SALE - Attention in the world barley market shifted to Brussels and Canada on Thursday as traders weighed up the cost of supplying 500,000 tonnes of barley to Saudi Arabia for April and May in a deal clinched on Wednesday. Four companies were involved in the sale, traders said, with most observers estimating the price of the deal at $152 to $154 per tonne, including freight. A detailed breakdown of prices was not available, however, and is likely to be kept under wraps.
BARLEY TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission invited tenders for the supply of 25,000 metric tonnes of barley with a shipment date by May 20, 1997. Tenders close on April 15.
BARLEY TENDERS - South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.

WHEAT TENDERS - Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender Tuesday for two 34,000-tonne wheat shipments from the U.S., traders said Thursday. The two shipments are slated for delivery from the PNW at April 25-May 15 and May 15-June 5.
- USDA's Commodity Credit Corp said it will tender April 15 to buy 25,470 tonnes dark northern spring wheat for donation to Ghana. The wheat was due for May 1-25 shipment.

RICE TENDER - Costa Rica will be tendering on April 30 for 26,500 tonnes optional origin long grain rough rice or 18,000 tonnes long grain milled rice, U.S. number 3 or equivalent, maximum 15 percent broken, exporters and traders said. The rice was slated for June 30-July 7 arrival. But one exporter said offers have to be in by April 16 rather than April 30.
- Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.

VEGOIL TENDER - El Salvador was seeking about 4,500 to 5,500 tonnes of U.S. vegoil under the PL-480 Title I export program, according to its shipping agent, International Services Corp. The vegoil included prime bleachable summer yellow (PBSY) cottonseed oil in bulk and/or refined bleached deodorized soybean oil in bulk. Shipping dates were slated for April 21-May 6. Offers are to be received no later than April 14 and all offers must remain valid through April 15.

TALLOW TENDER - El Salvador was tendering for about 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes of U.S. tallow in bulk under the PL-480 Title I export program, its shipping agent said. Shipment was set for April 21-May 6. Offers are to be received no later than April 14 and all offers must remain valid through April 15.

SOYMEAL TENDER - El Salvador was tendering for about 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean meal in bulk under the PL-480, Title I export program for April 21-May 6 delivery. Offers are to be received by April 14.

MARKET TALK - Egypt is under no pressure to buy wheat but the intentions of its unpredictable official commodities buyer are hard to gauge. European exporters had said they expected Egypt back into the world grain market soon to buy wheat for May and June but traders said nobody could predict what Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the General Authority for Supply Commodities, would do.
